analyzedSources.bodySummary: Explains oily, combination, dry and sensitive patterns by facial areas and connects the descriptions to what readers can see in a mirror.

Covers dry-skin causes, general care, and the point at which recurring or severe concerns can merit support from a clinician.
Frames lightweight hydration as relevant for oily and acne-prone routines while demonstrating how quickly search results move into product advice.
Describes a reader-recognisable mix of surface shine, tightness and rough-feeling areas, flagging harsh cleansing as a possible routine factor.
Separates oil and water in consumer language and recommends simplifying instead of escalating a routine when skin feels uncomfortable.
Uses balanced oil and moisture language and promotes gentle daily care, offering a useful contrast to more aggressive routine claims.
Adds India climate and texture context but makes broad causal and outcome claims that the MyMirror page must not repeat as evidence.
Positions sebum as type and hydration as a fluctuating condition, adding urban climate examples but with unsupported clinical framing.
